 Ford recalls over 102,000 F-Series pickups over faulty speedometer
 By Jason Gunn FOX Local Recalls Published  October 22, 2026 8:02 AM CDT Share
 Copy Link 
 Email 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Reddit 
 Published  October 22, 2026 8:02 AM CDT article The brand logo and the lettering of the car manufacturer Ford can be seen on the facade of a branch of the company in Munich (Bavaria) on August 29, 2025. (Photo by Matthias Balk/picture alliance via Getty Images) 
 The Brief
 Ford Motor Company is recalling more than 102,000 vehicles due to a defect with the vehicle's speedometer. 
 The recall impacts certain models of their F-Series pickup trucks from 2025-2026. 
 The vehicle's analog cluster's tachometer and speedometer may become stuck or move erratically and show the wrong speed, which would raise the risk of a crash. 
 Ford Motor Company is recalling more than 102,000 vehicles due to a defect with the vehicle's speedometer. 
 What we know:
 The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) says the recall impacts certain models of their F-Series pickup trucks from 2025-2026. 
 The recall notice says the analog cluster's tachometer and speedometer may become stuck or move erratically and show the wrong speed, which would raise the risk of a crash. 
 RELATED: Ford recalls more than 40,000 trucks and SUVs over visibility risk 
 The recall covers certain 2025-2026 F-250 SD, F-350 SD, F-450 SD, F-550 â€‹SD, â€‹F-600, â and 2026 F-150 and F-750 â€‹SD trucks. 
 Dig deeper:
 The issue was discovered in May when it was brought to review by Ford's Critical Concern Review Group. Ford concluded supplier process deficiencies caused the inaccurate readings. 
 As of September 16, 2026, Ford has identified 18 warranty and 93 field reports caused by the faulty equipment since January 2025. However, no accidents, fires or injuries have been reported. 
 RELATED: Over 11,000 Ford pickups recalled due to a possibly counterfeit component 
 Dealers will be able to replace the instrument cluster models for owners at no charge. 
 What's next:
 Owners are expected to be notified of the issue and risk when interim letters are mailed out on October 26, 2026. The automaker anticipates a permanent remedy to be available by the end of the year. 
 The Source: This story was written with information provided by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration and Reuters. This story was reported from Orlando.
